item.title: Trump pauses Iran strikes, warns of escalation if no deal
item.description: Iran confirmed on Wednesday that it is formally evaluating a US peace proposal as the two sides inch toward what a Pakistani mediator has described as a potential agreement to end the nearly 10-week war. President Donald Trump announced a temporary pause of "Project Freedom," the US military operation to reopen the Strait of Hormuz, citing "great progress" toward a deal — but warned that bombing would resume "at a much higher level and intensity" if Tehran refuses to come to terms.

item.title: China's Big Fund in talks to lead DeepSeek round at $45B valuation
item.description:
China's largest state-backed semiconductor investment vehicle is in advanced negotiations to lead the first external funding round for AI startup DeepSeek at a valuation of approximately $45 billion, the Financial Times reported on Tuesday, citing four people familiar with the discussions.

The China Integrated Circuit Industry Investment Fund — known in the industry as the "Big Fund" — would mark a dramatic expansion of its mandate, which has historically focused on chip fabrication, memory producers, and semiconductor equipment rather than AI model labs.

item.title: French container ship hit by missile in Strait of Hormuz
item.description:
French shipping giant CMA CGM confirmed on Wednesday that its Maltese-flagged container vessel, the CMA CGM San Antonio, was struck during an attack while transiting the Strait of Hormuz on Tuesday, injuring several crew members and damaging the ship.

U.S. officials told CBS News the vessel was hit by what they described as a possible land-attack cruise missile late Tuesday evening local time, with several Filipino crew members among the injured. The wounded were evacuated and are receiving medical treatment, the company said in a statement to AFP.

item.title: North Korea drops reunification from constitution, codifies Kim's nuclear authority
item.description:
North Korea has revised its constitution to remove all references to reunification with South Korea, formally codifying leader Kim Jong Un's doctrine of treating the two Koreas as hostile, separate states, according to a draft of the amended text reviewed by Reuters.

The revision, believed to have been adopted during a March session of the Supreme People's Assembly, marks the first time North Korea has included a territorial clause in its constitution, Seoul National University professor Lee Jung-chul said at a South Korean Unification Ministry briefing on Wednesday.

item.title: Ukraine says Russia violated ceasefire with overnight strikes
item.description: Ukraine accused Russia on Wednesday of breaching the unilateral ceasefire declared by President Volodymyr Zelenskyy, with Russian forces launching 108 drones and three missiles at Ukrainian territory in the hours after the truce took effect at midnight on the night of May 5-6.

item.title: Ted Turner, CNN founder and media mogul, dies at 87
item.description: Ted Turner, the maverick media mogul who founded CNN and transformed the landscape of American television, died Wednesday at age 87, according to Turner Enterprises. Turner, who had been living with Lewy body dementia since 2018, died at his home near Tallahassee, Florida.

item.title: Ted Turner, CNN founder and media mogul, dies at 87
item.description: Ted Turner, the brash media entrepreneur who launched the world's first 24-hour cable news network and reshaped how Americans consumed television, died Wednesday at age 87, according to Turner Enterprises. Turner died at his home near Tallahassee, Florida.

item.title: Shipping industry balks at Hormuz transit despite IRGC safe-passage pledge
item.description: Shipping companies are holding firm against resuming normal transits through the Strait of Hormuz, even as Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps announced "new protocols" for safe passage and signs of a potential U.S.-Iran peace agreement emerge following President Trump's pause of military operations in the waterway.

item.title: US, Iran near 14-point memo to end Gulf war, awaiting Tehran's response
item.description: Iran confirmed on Wednesday that it is evaluating a new 14-point US proposal aimed at ending the more than two-month-long Gulf conflict, even as President Donald Trump warned that military action could resume at a higher intensity if Tehran rejects the terms.

item.title: Trump says Iran must send enriched uranium to US in deal
item.description: President Donald Trump confirmed Wednesday that Iran's enriched uranium would be transferred to the United States as part of an emerging agreement to end the war, saying "No, not perhaps. It goes to the United States" when asked in a PBS News interview about the possibility of Tehran exporting its highly enriched nuclear material.

item.title: Iran's Ghalibaf vows nation 'will not surrender' amid US naval blockade
item.description:
Iran's Parliament Speaker and top negotiator Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf issued an audio message to the Iranian public on Wednesday accusing Washington of deploying a naval blockade, sanctions, and media manipulation to force Tehran into capitulation, as the country's economy buckles under the weight of a three-week-old maritime siege.

"The enemy is trying to dismantle internal cohesion through economic pressure and psychological warfare," Ghalibaf said, according to remarks carried by Iran's Fars news agency. He described the current moment as one of the most critical periods in Iran's modern history and said Washington was acting on "false intelligence" that would ultimately "cause everyone to suffer".

item.title: U.S. jet disables Iranian tanker defying naval blockade
item.description:
A U.S. Navy F/A-18 Super Hornet fired 20mm cannon rounds into the rudder of an Iranian-flagged oil tanker on Wednesday, disabling the vessel as it attempted to reach an Iranian port in defiance of the American naval blockade, U.S. Central Command confirmed.

The incident, which occurred at 9 a.m. ET on May 6, marks the second time U.S. forces have used direct fire to stop a vessel from breaching the blockade since it began on April 13.

item.title: North Korea declares it is not bound by nuclear treaty
item.description:
North Korea's top United Nations diplomat declared on Thursday that Pyongyang is not bound by the Nuclear Non-Proliferation Treaty under any circumstances, reinforcing the country's insistence on being recognized as a nuclear weapons state during a major international conference in New York.

Ambassador Kim Song, North Korea's permanent representative to the UN, made the statement at the 11th NPT Review Conference, which is taking place at UN headquarters from April 27 to May 22. Kim criticized the United States and other Western nations for what he described as attempts to degrade the conference's atmosphere by raising the issue of North Korea's nuclear arsenal, according to state media outlet KCNA.

item.title: Three U.S. states monitor residents from hantavirus cruise ship
item.description: Health authorities in at least three U.S. states are monitoring residents who traveled aboard the MV Hondius, a Dutch cruise ship at the center of a deadly hantavirus outbreak that has killed three passengers and sickened several others during an Atlantic voyage. None of the monitored individuals have shown symptoms, officials said Wednesday.

item.title: Saudi airbase threat forced Trump to pause Project Freedom
item.description:
President Donald Trump's abrupt suspension of "Project Freedom" — the US naval operation to escort commercial ships through the Strait of Hormuz — came after Saudi Arabia threatened to deny American military aircraft access to Prince Sultan Airbase and Saudi airspace, according to two US officials cited by NBC News.

The revelation offers a starkly different explanation from Trump's public framing of the pause, which he attributed to Pakistan's mediation and "great progress" toward a deal with Iran.

item.title: NATO scrambles jets after drones from Russia crash in Latvia
item.description:
Two drones entered NATO member Latvia from Russian territory early Thursday morning and crashed in the eastern Latgale region, with one striking an oil storage facility in the city of Rēzekne about 40 kilometers from the Russian border, according to the Latvian army.

Latvia's Defence Minister Andris Spruds told national broadcaster LSM that the drones were "probably launched by Ukraine against targets in Russia," suggesting they may have veered off course — possibly due to electronic warfare jamming — before entering Latvian airspace. No casualties were reported.

item.title: Trump hosts Lula at White House for tariff, minerals talks
item.description: President Donald Trump is welcoming Brazilian President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva to the White House on Thursday for a working meeting that spans tariffs, organized crime cooperation, and access to Brazil's vast rare earth mineral reserves. The encounter marks the first in-person bilateral meeting on American soil since Trump returned to office and the most consequential diplomatic moment of Lula's third term.

item.title: Russia tells diplomats to evacuate Kyiv ahead of May 9
item.description: Russia's Foreign Ministry on Wednesday issued a formal warning to all foreign diplomatic missions and international organizations in Kyiv, urging them to evacuate personnel ahead of possible large-scale strikes on the Ukrainian capital tied to the May 9 Victory Day commemorations.

item.title: Rubio meets Pope Leo XIV amid Trump-Vatican feud
item.description:
U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio arrived in Rome on Thursday for a high-stakes diplomatic visit aimed at easing weeks of tension between the Trump administration, the Vatican, and the Italian government. Rubio is scheduled to meet Pope Leo XIV at the Vatican's Apostolic Palace on the morning of May 7, followed by meetings on Friday with Italian Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni and Foreign Minister Antonio Tajani.

The visit amounts to a diplomatic cleanup mission after President Donald Trump's escalating feud with the first American-born pope rattled relations with two of Washington's most important partners in Europe.

item.title: Saudi Arabia, Kuwait restore U.S. military base access after Hormuz standoff
item.description: Saudi Arabia and Kuwait have lifted restrictions on U.S. military use of their bases and airspace, according to The Wall Street Journal, removing a major obstacle that had forced President Donald Trump to suspend his "Project Freedom" naval escort operation in the Strait of Hormuz just days ago.
